blocks.text: Mastering Slack navigation on your Mac

Efficiency starts with your keyboard. Stop clicking through sidebars to find your channels. Use Command + K to open the Quick Switcher. Type the first few letters of a channel or person to jump there instantly. This saves seconds every time you switch contexts. If you have many workspaces, use Command + Shift + [ or ] to cycle through them.

items: Command + / opens the full list of keyboard shortcuts.
Command + , opens your preferences to adjust notification sounds.
Command + F searches the current channel for specific keywords.
Command + G opens the global search bar for everything.

blocks.text: Support work involves constant incoming messages. You need control over when you are interrupted. Open your profile menu to set a Do Not Disturb schedule. This lets you focus on complex tickets without alerts. If you miss important messages, check your system settings. Go to System Settings > Notifications > Slack and ensure banners are enabled. You can also use /dnd in any channel to pause alerts for a specific duration.

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you handle Slack tasks without taking your hands off the keyboard. Hold the fn key to dictate your technical responses directly into the Slack message box. This is faster than typing long explanations for customers. If you are stuck on a setting, hold Option + Command and ask Lazur where a specific menu item is located. It will circle the button on your screen.

Use sections in your sidebar to group channels by priority. Right-click a channel and move it to a custom section like Urgent or Product Feedback. This keeps your main view clear. For messages that require action later, hover over the message and click the Save icon. You can view these later in the Saved items section at the top of your sidebar. Never let a support ticket slip through the cracks because it was buried in a busy channel.

If Slack feels slow or images fail to load, clear your cache. Go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This resets the app data and often fixes performance issues. Ensure you are running macOS 14 or higher for the best compatibility. Slack updates its requirements twice a year in May and November. Keep your app version 4.53.x or newer to avoid bugs.

faq.question: How do I jump to a channel quickly?
faq.answer: Press Command + K to open the Quick Switcher, then type the channel name.

faq.question: Can I format text in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes, use Command + B for bold and Command + I for italics. Use Shift + Enter to add a new line without sending.

faq.question: What should I do if Slack is slow?
faq.answer: Navigate to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart to refresh your app data.
